[[File:Pepsi Center inside.jpg|300px|thumb|The Avalanche have played their home games at [[Ball Arena]] since 1999.]]
The [[Colorado Avalanche]] are an American professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Denver]]. They play in the [[Central Division (NHL)|Central Division]] of the [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090311030113/http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 11, 2009|title=Teams|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=2008-12-26}}</ref> The team joined the NHL in 1972 as a charter member of the [[World Hockey Association]], and were named the [[Quebec Nordiques]], but moved to Denver in 1995. The Avalanche won their first [[Stanley Cup]] [[List of Stanley Cup champions|championship]] in 1996, and won another one in 2001.<ref name="history">{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsline.com/nhl/teams/history/COL|title=Colorado Avalanche History|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |work=[[CBSSports.com]] |accessdate= 2008-12-26}}</ref> Having first played at the [[McNichols Sports Arena]], the Avalanche have played their home games at [[Ball Arena]] (formerly the Pepsi Center) since 1999.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pepsicenter.com/Facility/ArenaFacts/Default.aspx|title=Arena Facts|publisher=[[Pepsi Center]]|accessdate=2008-12-26|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218204738/http://www.pepsicenter.com/Facility/ArenaFacts/Default.aspx|archivedate=2008-12-18}}</ref> The Avalanche are owned by [[Ann Walton Kroenke]], their [[general manager]] is  [[Chris MacFarland]], [[Joe Sakic]] was named president of hockey operations in 2022. [[Gabriel Landeskog]] is the team [[Captain (ice hockey)|captain]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://avalanche.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=Tea_Staff|title=Team - Coaching & Staff|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=2008-12-26|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081217095910/http://avalanche.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=Tea_Staff|archivedate=2008-12-17}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://avalanche.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=TeamPlayers&type=roster|title=Roster|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=2008-12-26|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081228033638/http://avalanche.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=TeamPlayers&type=roster|archivedate=2008-12-28}}</ref>

There have been seven&nbsp;[[head coach]]es for the Avalanche team. The team's first head coach was [[Marc Crawford]], who coached for three seasons. None of the Avalanche head coaches have been elected into the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] as a [[List of members of the Hockey Hall of Fame#Builders|builder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Builder|title=Builders by Induction Year|publisher=[[Hockey Hall of Fame]]|accessdate=2008-12-26|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090528120538/http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Builder|archivedate=2009-05-28}}</ref> [[Tony Granato]], who coached two terms with the Avalanche, has spent his entire NHL head coaching career with the Avalanche. Granato was fired after the [[2008–09 NHL season|2008–09 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.canada.com/Sherman+named+Granato+fired+coach/1658996/story.html|title=Sherman named Avs' GM, Granato fired as coach|publisher=Canwest|date=2009-06-03|accessdate=2009-06-03}}</ref>

On June 4, 2009, the Avalanche hired [[Joe Sacco (ice hockey)|Joe Sacco]], the coach of their AHL affiliate The Lake Erie Monsters, as the new head coach to succeed Granato.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=4230979|title=Avs hire AHL coach Sacco|publisher=Associated Press|date=2009-06-04|access-date=2010-04-24}}</ref> Following the [[2012-13 NHL season|2012–13]] season, his fourth year at the helm, finishing last in the Western Conference and out of the playoffs for a third consecutive year, Sacco was relieved of his duties on April 28, 2013.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.denverpost.com/avalanche/ci_23126661/joe-sacco-fired-coach-colorado-avalanche |title=Sacco fired as coach of Colorado Avalanche after four NHL seasons |newspaper=[[Denver Post]] |date=2013-04-28 |accessdate=2013-04-28 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130429054706/http://www.denverpost.com/avalanche/ci_23126661/joe-sacco-fired-coach-colorado-avalanche |archivedate=2013-04-29 }}</ref>

A month later, former Avalanche goalie [[Patrick Roy]] was introduced as the team's latest head coach on May 28, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nhl/2013/5/28/4373662/patrick-roy-colorado-avalanche-coach|title=Patrick Roy introduced as Avalanche head coach, vice president of hockey operations|publisher=SB Nation|date=2013-05-28|accessdate=2013-05-28}}</ref> On August 11, 2016, Roy announced that he had resigned as head coach of the Avalanche.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.denverpost.com/2016/08/11/patrick-roy-out-colorado-avalanche-coach/|title=Patrick Roy quits as Colorado Avalanche coach|newspaper=Denver Post|date=2016-08-11|accessdate=2017-07-18}}</ref>

On August 25, 2016, [[Jared Bednar]] was announced as the seventh head coach in Avalanche history.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.denverpost.com/2016/08/25/jared-bednar-hired-colorado-avalanche-head-coach/|title=Jared Bednar selected as new Colorado Avalanche head coach|newspaper=Denver Post|date=2016-08-25|accessdate=2017-07-18}}</ref>

Crawford, Hartley and Bednar are the only head coaches to have won the [[Stanley Cup]] with the Avalanche, in the [[1996 Stanley Cup Final]], the [[2001 Stanley Cup Final]] and the [[2022 Stanley Cup Final]] respectively.

==Notes==
